title: The point, evaluated
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient data and a six-functor datum as in [def-sf-datum], with $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Use the small pro-etale point coefficient categories and evaluation functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, and $\omega_s=Ra_s^!\Lambda_s$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme with structure map $a_X:X\to s$, as required for the operations in the datum and the cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Then:

1. $\omega_s\cong\Lambda_s$.
2. For every $C\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, evaluation identifies its internal dual with its coefficient dual $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$ of [def-pod-perfect-point-complex]:
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s\bigl(R\mathcal H om_s(C,\omega_s)\bigr)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda\bigl(\operatorname{Fib}_s C,\Lambda\bigr).$$
3. $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is an exact equivalence from $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ to the corresponding point category $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, or the common-stage $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$, hence conservative.
4. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$,
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}K)=R\Gamma_c(X,K),\qquad \operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X*}K)=R\Gamma(X,K).$$
5. For every $C\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$ there is the natural identification
$$H^r(\operatorname{Fib}_s C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(s,\Lambda)}(\Lambda_s[-r],C).$$
At the algebraically closed coefficient stage, coefficient duals are interpreted at common finite stages, and $H^r$ is the colimit of the finite-stage cohomology vector spaces under scalar extension to $\Qlb$, as in [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]; the source's formulas omitting $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ use the equivalence in (3).

proof.text: The datum [def-sf-datum] supplies $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ by (A1) and proper coincidence by (A4). The identity $a_s$ is proper and its ordinary direct image is the identity, hence $Ra_{s!}\cong\mathrm{id}$. Write $G=Ra_s^!$ and transport the adjunction to $\mathrm{id}\dashv G$. Its unit and counit are $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to G$ and $\varepsilon:G\to\mathrm{id}$. The first triangle gives $\varepsilon_C\eta_C=1_C$. The other gives $G(\varepsilon_C)\eta_{G C}=1_{G C}$; naturality of $\eta$ identifies its left side with $\eta_C\varepsilon_C$. Thus $\eta_C$ and $\varepsilon_C$ are inverse, naturally in $C$, and $G\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_s$.

Take the auxiliary $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ in [def-pod-conventions]. Its structure map is the identity: the affine algebra is $k_0$ with an empty finite presentation and the unique lift in every infinitesimal lifting square, so it is smooth; its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence closed, and it is finite type. After any field extension $L/k_0$, the base change is $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with only the zero prime, hence connected of dimension zero. In particular its base change to $k$ is $s$, with identity structure map.

For this auxiliary point, the identity compactification is exceptional-adjoint admissible: full cohomological dimension, interval bounds, finite-Tor preservation, identity adjunction data, and all coefficient/refinement comparisons are supplied by [lem-sf-point-identity-admissibility].

For the auxiliary point of steps 2--3, the hypotheses of [def-pod-conventions] hold. Apply [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]: with $V=\operatorname{Fib}_sC$ it gives $\operatorname{Fib}_s(D_sC)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(V,\Lambda)$. This is a point-only calculation and imposes no condition on the given $X$.
At the point, [def-pod-conventions] uses the same four coefficient categories as [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and writes $A$ for the selected coefficient ring, hence this $A$ is our $\Lambda$.

By [def-pod-perfect-point-complex], $C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(C,\Lambda)$; the dual definition has no perfectness hypothesis. By [def-sf-datum], the datum's exceptional inverse image and internal Hom are the operation-datum functors, so $\omega_s=\omega_{s,\Lambda}$ and $R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_s)=D_sC$.

The exact equivalence statement for evaluation is [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. An equivalence is conservative, and the cited statement also records preservation of shifts and distinguished triangles, hence exactness in the triangulated point categories.

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, the definitions in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] are exactly $R\Gamma_c(X,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}K)$ and $R\Gamma(X,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X*}K)$, giving the two displayed global-section identifications.

The exact equivalence of [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] and the coefficient-unit identification in [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] give $\operatorname{Hom}_s(\Lambda_s[-r],C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Lambda)}(\Lambda[-r],V)$ for $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s C$ at a finite, integral or rational stage. Here the point targets are full subcategories of their module derived categories, as specified by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Compute the latter Hom group using [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection]. The complex $P=\Lambda[-r]$ is K-projective directly: a chain map $P\to N$ into an acyclic complex is a cycle $z\in N^r$, and $z=d y$ yields a null-homotopy by sending $1$ to $y\in N^{r-1}$. Consequently derived maps from $P$ are chain maps modulo homotopy. A chain map $P\to V$ is exactly a cycle in degree $r$; two such maps are homotopic exactly when their cycles differ by a boundary. Their quotient is $H^r(V)$ by [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]. A chain map of targets sends $z$ to its image and $d y$ to the boundary of the image of $y$, so this bijection is natural in $V$. This also fixes the shift sign. At $\Qlb$, use the Hom-colimit definition of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]: represent $C$ and the unit at a common finite extension, apply the field-stage calculation, and pass to that directed colimit. Its transition is scalar extension and has $H^r(TV)=H^r(V)\otimes L$, as stated in that definition, so the Hom colimit is $\varinjlim_{L\supseteq E}H^r(V_E)\otimes_E L=H^r(V_E)\otimes_E\Qlb$, exactly $H^r(V)$ by [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules]. The stagewise naturality just checked commutes with these scalar-extension transitions, so it descends to the asserted natural identification.
